summary: Provides _CallerInput, a proxy around a caller-supplied input stream used during uploads. It delegates every attribute unchanged while recording exceptions raised by the caller's stream. original_in() walks an exception's __cause__/__context__ chain to find a recorded caller error, so write backends can re-raise the caller's own exception instead of reclassifying it as a backend failure.
key_classes: _CallerInput(source) — attribute-delegating proxy that records exceptions raised by caller-owned stream methods for one transfer
key_functions: _CallerInput.original_in(error) -> (exception, traceback) | None — search error's cause/context graph for a recorded caller exception
extension_points: Write backends that hand a caller stream to an SDK which may wrap its exceptions (boto3 managed upload, httpx) should wrap the stream in _CallerInput and consult original_in() before mapping errors
lifecycle_notes: One instance per transfer; recorded errors are retained only for that transfer
Records BaseException, including KeyboardInterrupt and attribute lookup failures
documentation_hooks: README 'Storage errors' contract: caller input failures are not reclassified as backend failures
Maintainer note on preserving caller exception identity across SDK-managed uploads
risks: No dedicated unit test file; behaviour is covered only through S3 and HTTP backend tests (test_s3_managed_upload_preserves_colliding_caller_error, test_s3_wrapped_input_failure_restores_caller_cause, test_http_caller_error_keeps_identity)
Proxying via __getattr__ means isinstance checks and dunder protocol lookups (e.g. iteration) on the proxy do not reach the source stream; SDKs that type-check inputs may behave differently
Matching uses object identity; an SDK that re-creates rather than wraps the exception defeats recovery
open_questions: SFTP has a caller-input test (tests/storage/backends/test_sftp.py::test_sftp_caller_input_failure_is_unchanged) but does not use _CallerInput; is that intentional because paramiko does not wrap caller errors?
